content.title: Xbox Series X: Is the Console Still Worth It in 2026?
content.text: With Microsoft announcing the Xbox Next, the question is coming up more often: is it still worth buying an Xbox Series X in 2026? We’ve gathered all the info you need. The Xbox Series X has been on the market since late 2020 and established itself as one of the most powerful consoles of its generation. But now it’s 2026 – and many of you are wondering: should you still pick up a Series X, or wait for the next generation (Xbox Next)? Let’s take a step-by-step look at performance, games, pricing, and what the future holds. Hardware & Performance: Still High-End? Even in 2026, the hardware of the Xbox Series X remains impressive. You still get: Native 4K resolution in many games Frame rates up to 120 FPS Ray tracing and Auto HDR Fast load times thanks to NVMe SSD The console comes in several versions, including the standard model with Blu-Ray drive, a digital-only edition, and special editions like the “Galaxy Black Special Edition” with 2 TB SSD. Compared to current consoles, the Series X is still at the top when it comes to overall performance and graphical quality. Of course, a high-end PC GPU is stronger, but in the console space the Series X, alongside the PlayStation 5, remains a powerhouse. Note: Sony has also announced its next-gen console. The PlayStation 6 is expected to launch around 2027. Pricing & Deals in 2026 When it comes to price, things have shifted quite a bit. Series X (1 TB, with disc drive): Around €550 to €599 Digital Edition: Around €500 Series S: Around €300 Deals and bundles often make it cheaper. The used market in 2026 is also worth a look: with the next generation approaching, prices are dropping, so you can often grab a second-hand console for €100–200 less. If you don’t mind minor wear, you’ll save quite a bit. Microsoft raised Xbox prices again in US market Microsoft in the United States increased the price for its Xbox Consoles last Year. The price hike affects both the Xbox Series S and the more powerful Xbox Series X models, with increases ranging from $20 to $70, representing a 5 to 10 percent jump. The Xbox Series S will now cost $329, up from its current price of $299. The Xbox Series X will see its price rise from $499 to between $549 and $569, depending on retailer recommendations. Microsoft attributes these changes to “shifts in the macroeconomic environment,” likely referring to new import tariffs in the United States. The price adjustment only applies to the US market, with other regions maintaining their current pricing. Additionally, the increase affects only the consoles themselves—accessories like controllers and headsets will keep their existing price points. For US customers, this marks the second price increase in just a few months, following a global price adjustment that occurred in May. Games & Game Pass: Still Plenty of Content Hardware is one thing – but games are what really matter. And 2026 looks very strong here as well. Microsoft continues to push Xbox Game Pass as a major selling point: hundreds of games for a monthly fee, including brand-new releases. Last Year there were some special Releases as well. Highlights of 2025 were: Borderlands 4 Hollow Knight: Silksong Hell is Us Plenty of remasters, action blockbusters, and next-gen optimized titles So support for current and upcoming games is secured. You don’t have to worry about running out of fresh content after buying a Series X. Looking Ahead: Xbox Next as the Better Alternative? A key factor in your decision is of course the upcoming next generation. According to leaks and rumors, Microsoft is planning a new console around 2027 with the following specs: Zen 6 CPU, RDNA 5 GPU Performance on par with an RTX 5080 – roughly 50% more power than the Series X 24–32 GB RAM Expected price between $600–800 Possibly a new modular design concept Important: None of this has been officially confirmed. What is clear, however, is that the leap will be noticeable but not revolutionary. So don’t expect a “next-gen shock.” The new console will also be significantly more expensive, making the Series X a very solid value right now. Who Should Still Buy the Series X? The answer depends a bit on what type of gamer you are: You want to enjoy current games right now in top console quality?→ Get the Series X. You don’t own a console yet and want an all-in-one device (gaming, apps, streaming, Blu-Ray)?→ Also makes sense. You care about price-performance and cheap access to Game Pass?→ In 2026, the Series X has dropped in price and is very attractive. You’re a hardcore tech enthusiast and only want the very latest hardware?→ Waiting for the Xbox Next might be worth it. Even after Xbox Next launches, the Series X won’t be shut down right away. Historically, Microsoft supports older consoles for years – so you’ll have peace of mind for the long run. Even games released in 2027 will most likely remain backwards compatible. First details and rumors about the new Xbox Next are known. © Microsoft Buying Used – Yes or No? The used market is a real argument in 2026. With anticipation building for the “Xbox Next,” many players are selling their Series X. If you stick to reliable sellers (retailers with warranty or platforms with buyer protection), you can get excellent value for money. Conclusion: Is the Xbox Series X Still Worth It in 2026? Bottom line: Yes, the Xbox Series X is still worth it in 2026. It remains one of the most powerful consoles on the market, continues to receive brand-new titles, offers an excellent ecosystem with Game Pass, and has become more attractive thanks to falling prices. Waiting only makes sense if you’re set on the next big leap in hardware and are ready to spend $600 to 800 or more for the Xbox Next. For everyone else, the Series X remains a top choice – whether as your first console, an upgrade from an older Xbox, or as a complement to a gaming PC.
